def _code_execution_runtime_observation(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Mint a host-side runtime observation for durable code execution.

        This producer is deliberately separate from the Java return value:
        release/build comes from the existing exact model-delivery helper and
        Worker/server identity is compared with the live backend binding.
        Failure leaves a durable UNVERIFIED marker and does not rewrite the
        terminal outcome of the already-completed code execution.
        """
        observation: dict[str, Any] = {
            "schema": "comsol-worker-runtime-observation/v1",
            "status": "UNVERIFIED",
        }
        try:
            from ._g3_model_delivery import _current_version
            from ._runtime_installation import runtime_id_for_root

            worker = self.worker
            service = self.service
            paths = getattr(worker, "paths", None)
            root = getattr(paths, "comsol_root", None)
            if root is None or service is None:
                raise ValueError("attached Worker installation or service is unavailable")
            version = _current_version(worker)
            runtime_id = runtime_id_for_root(root)
            identity = self.worker_identity
            health = worker.runtime_metadata()
            required = {
                "runtime_id": runtime_id,
                "worker_instance_id": health.get("instance_id") if isinstance(health, Mapping) else None,
                "connection_epoch": health.get("generation") if isinstance(health, Mapping) else None,
                "server_instance_id": service.ledger.server_instance_id,
                "endpoint": self.endpoint_key,
            }
            if (not isinstance(identity, Mapping) or any(identity.get(name) != value for name, value in required.items())
                    or not isinstance(health, Mapping) or health.get("connected") is not True
                    or health.get("server") != self.endpoint_key
                    or type(required["connection_epoch"]) is not int or required["connection_epoch"] < 1
                    or not all(isinstance(required[name], str) and required[name]
                               for name in ("runtime_id", "worker_instance_id", "server_instance_id", "endpoint"))):
                raise ValueError("live Worker identity differs from the backend binding")
            observation.update({"status": "OBSERVED", "comsol_version": version,
                                "runtime_identity": required})
        except Exception as exc:
            observation.update({"reason_code": getattr(exc, "code", None) or "RUNTIME_IDENTITY_UNVERIFIED",
                                "cause_type": type(exc).__name__})
        return observation

#: The Java signature of the varargs parameter ``ModelUtil.hasProduct(String...)``
#: declares.  Sending the argument as a declared ``String[]`` value is what makes
#: the call marshal: a bare scalar cannot be converted to the one array parameter
#: the method declares, and the Worker then refuses the overload.
STRING_ARRAY_SIGNATURE = "java.lang.String[]"


def string_array_value(values: Sequence[str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Pack ``values`` as a declared Java ``String[]`` argument.

    The typed-value form (``kind``/``shape``/``data``/``java_signature``) is the
    contract the Worker's marshaller reads: ``java_signature`` is matched against
    the parameter type of the overload it is offered to, so a signature mistake
    is refused instead of being silently coerced, and ``data`` is the array
    contents.  A ``String...`` parameter is one ``String[]`` parameter, which is
    why the caller of e.g. ``hasProduct`` cannot pass a bare string.
    """
    items = [str(item) for item in values]
    return {
        "kind": "string",
        "shape": [len(items)],
        "data": items,
        "java_signature": STRING_ARRAY_SIGNATURE,
    }


def _facade_argument(value: Any) -> Any:
    """Unwrap a declared ``String[]`` value for a Python client facade.

it cannot be the identity of the runtime that answered.  This block reports
    the observed Worker identity instead (instance id, connection epoch and
    generation) and states that neither a bound model nor a model revision was
    required, because a runtime capability question is not a model operation.
    """
    identity = _worker_identity(worker)
    instance = identity.get("instance_id")
    bound_id = f"runtime-{instance}" if isinstance(instance, str) and instance else None
    metadata = dict(identity)
    metadata["runtime_id"] = bound_id
    metadata["runtime_id_source"] = "PersistentJavaWorker.runtime_metadata().instance_id"
    metadata["revision_dependency"] = {
        "required": False,
        "reason": "a runtime capability query is not bound to a model revision",
    }
    metadata["bound_model_required"] = False
    return metadata
